before.title: R1T / R1S Charge Port Motor / Door Failure
before.description: Multiple owner reports of the charge port door motor failing — door refuses to open via app/touchscreen/button, sometimes stuck open after charge session. Cold weather amplifies failure rate. Rivian replaces under warranty; some early VINs received recall for related door-latch behavior.
before.solution: Service center charge port assembly replacement under warranty. Out-of-warranty $400-$700. Owners can sometimes manually push the door (gently) to free a stuck door — emergency release procedure in owner's manual.

proposal.title: R1T / R1S Charge Port Motor / Door Failure
proposal.description: The frozen page has no citation supporting a common charge-port motor or door failure across 2022-2024 R1T/R1S vehicles, a cold-weather failure-rate increase or an early-VIN recall. Rivian's owner guides confirm normal charge-port-door operation and a manual release for a charge plug that will not disconnect; that cable does not establish an emergency release for a stuck door or diagnose a failed door motor. A door that will not open, a door that will not close and a connector that will not release are separate failure paths.
proposal.solution: Confirm whether the problem is the door, its sensor/actuator, the charge connector lock or the charging session. Follow the owner guide to stop charging and use only the documented plug-release procedure when the connector itself will not release. Do not push or force the powered door. Capture messages and contact Rivian service for diagnosis if the door cannot operate normally. Do not buy a motor or charge-port assembly from this page; the failed component, generation and calibration state are unresolved.
symptoms: Charge-port door does not open or close normally
Charge connector remains locked after the session is stopped
affectedSystems: Charge-port door actuator and sensor, exact fault unresolved
Charge connector lock, separate failure path

before.title: Early R1T Upper Control Arm Corrosion (Salt-Belt)
before.description: Early R1T owners in salt-belt regions (US Northeast/Midwest, Canada) report surprising rapid surface corrosion on the upper control arms — bare metal exposed at welds, bushings showing rust through finish. Rivian made running production changes around mid-2023. Affected cars eligible for inspection.
before.solution: Schedule Rivian service inspection — many cars have been replaced under warranty for early-onset corrosion. Annual underbody wash strongly recommended. Aftermarket undercoating shops can treat at owner expense ($400-$800).

proposal.title: Early R1T Upper Control Arm Corrosion (Salt-Belt)
proposal.description: The frozen page has no source establishing rapid upper-control-arm corrosion as a recurring 2022-2023 R1T defect, a mid-2023 production change or routine replacement eligibility. Rivian campaign RCA-46-22-001-1 addresses oversized shock-tower pass-through holes and possible upper-control-arm bushing wear in a narrow August-October 2021 build population; it does not address corrosion. Rivian's warranty guide separately describes corrosion-perforation coverage, which is not proof that visible surface rust is a covered structural defect.
proposal.solution: Photograph the exact location and progression after cleaning, and have Rivian inspect any flaking metal, section loss, cracked weld, loose bushing, alignment change or suspension noise. Follow the owner guide for washing and avoid coating fasteners, joints, drains or high-voltage components without written Rivian guidance. Do not buy a control arm, bushing or undercoating treatment from this page; surface condition, structural loss, campaign eligibility and warranty coverage require inspection.

before.description: Rivian issued a software action in 2022 covering R1T vehicles for a frunk (front trunk) auto-close obstacle-detection issue — the powered frunk could close on fingers when the detection didn't trigger correctly. Software-only remedy via OTA. Check the official Rivian recall lookup for current campaign status applicable to your VIN.
before.solution: Software update via OTA was the remedy. Confirm VIN via rivian.com/support/article/recall-information or the NHTSA recall lookup. If older software, plug in at home to download the OTA.

proposal.title: R1T Frunk Auto-Close Finger Pinch Recall (22V-176)
proposal.description: The campaign number in the frozen title is false for this identity: NHTSA 22V-176 belongs to Volkswagen rear suspension knuckles and is not a Rivian frunk recall. Rivian's R1T owner guide documents powered-hood operation and charge-plug access, but the captured official records do not establish a 2022 Rivian finger-pinch recall or OTA remedy. The page remains indexed as a hold because changing the title/slug requires an approved identity-and-redirect policy.
proposal.solution: Keep hands, children and objects clear of the powered hood whenever it moves, stop using it if obstacle detection or reversal behaves unexpectedly, and contact Rivian service with the VIN and software version. Do not test pinch protection with a body part or object and do not treat 22V-176 as Rivian recall eligibility. Do not buy a latch, sensor, strut or hood actuator from this page; no official Rivian campaign or failed component has been established for this identity.

before.title: R1T / R1S 12V Auxiliary Battery Drain (Gear Guard, Cellular Modem)
before.description: R1T and R1S report 12V drain after long parking — particularly with Gear Guard (cabin/exterior camera surveillance) enabled, which keeps cellular modem and cameras active. Owners report dead 12V in 7-14 days without Gear Guard, faster with it. Multiple OTA updates have improved parasitic draw but not eliminated.
before.solution: Update to latest software. Disable Gear Guard for long parking. Use a 12V battery maintainer for storage stretches over 2 weeks. AGM 12V replacement under warranty for early failures; out-of-warranty ~$250-$400.

proposal.title: R1T / R1S 12V Auxiliary Battery Drain (Gear Guard, Cellular Modem)
proposal.description: Rivian has issued targeted communications for 12 V battery service and a narrow 2022 R1T BMS-firmware campaign, but those records do not establish Gear Guard or the cellular modem as a universal cause, a seven-to-fourteen-day failure interval or incomplete OTA correction across all 2022-2024 R1T/R1S vehicles. A low-voltage warning, loss of vehicle access and a no-power condition can arise from battery state, hardware, wiring, charging control or software and must be diagnosed separately.
proposal.solution: Record the exact warning, software version, storage duration and whether the vehicle still responds. Follow Rivian's current owner-guide and service instructions; if Rivian sends a 12 V service notice, schedule the identified service promptly. A no-access/no-power vehicle may require Rivian roadside support. Do not attach an unapproved maintainer or jump equipment unless the applicable guide specifically permits the procedure. Do not buy a 12 V battery, BMS or modem from this page; generation, cause and service eligibility require VIN-level diagnosis.

before.title: R1T / R1S Quad-Motor Front Drive Unit Failures
before.description: Early-production Quad-Motor R1T and R1S (2022-2023) have documented front drive unit failures — typically presenting as a grinding/whining noise, vehicle warnings about drive system, or sudden loss of front-axle drive. Rivian has replaced many under warranty; reports cluster around 20,000-40,000 miles. Quad-Motor architecture (separate motors per wheel) means a single DU failure leaves three working motors but with warning lights.
before.solution: Rivian warranty replacement is the standard fix (8 yr / 175,000 mi powertrain). Document any noise or warning promptly. Out-of-warranty drive unit replacement is dealer-only and likely $4,000-$8,000 per unit.

proposal.title: R1T / R1S Quad-Motor Front Drive Unit Failures
proposal.description: Exact Rivian communications support narrower conditions than the frozen page. RCA-38-22-002-1 covers some 2022 R1Ts built January-March 2022 with under-torqued front and/or rear drive-unit housing fasteners. RCA-38-23-003-2 covers some 2022 R1T/R1S vehicles with sealing-plug damage that can leak fluid and eventually reduce drive-unit life. These records do not establish recurring Quad-Motor front-unit failures across 2022-2024, a 20,000-40,000-mile cluster or the claim that any one failure always leaves three motors available.
proposal.solution: Record warning text, noise, vibration, leak location and the operating state, then contact Rivian. A reduced-performance indicator, fluid leak or new grinding/whining needs prompt service; do not rely on presumed remaining-motor operation. Rivian should determine whether a VIN-specific campaign, plug repair, fastener retorque or drive-unit repair applies. Warranty coverage depends on the applicable warranty and vehicle history. Do not buy a drive unit, plug or fluid from this page; axle, unit, cause and VIN eligibility are unresolved.
symptoms: Fluid observed near a drive unit

before.title: R1T / R1S Infotainment Freezes + Black-Screen Reboots
before.description: R1T and R1S center display and driver display can freeze, reboot mid-drive, or go black entirely — particularly during cellular handoffs (entering/leaving tunnel), after wake from sleep, or during OTA installation. Loss of driver display means losing speed/range readout in motion (workaround: use HUD if equipped or phone). Multiple OTA releases have improved but not eliminated.
before.solution: Hard reset: hold both scroll wheels on steering wheel 10+ seconds. Severe cases require service center module replacement. Stay on latest software (OTA). Some owners disable Gear Guard to reduce modem-related reboots.

proposal.title: R1T / R1S Infotainment Freezes + Black-Screen Reboots
proposal.description: Rivian documented a specific infotainment problem associated with the 2023.42 software update and later announced a remote fix. That evidence does not establish that cellular handoffs, sleep/wake behavior, Gear Guard or OTA installation universally cause freezes across all 2022-2024 R1T/R1S vehicles, nor does it support the frozen module-replacement claim. A frozen center display, driver display and update failure are distinct diagnostic states.
proposal.solution: If a display freezes or goes black, maintain control of the vehicle, pull over safely when required information is unavailable, record which display and software version are affected, and follow Rivian's current support instructions. Install only official updates and contact Rivian if the condition persists or safety information is unavailable. Do not assume Gear Guard is the cause and do not buy a display or infotainment module from this page; software state, display, controller and power supply require diagnosis.
symptoms: Center display freezes or goes black
Infotainment remains unavailable after an official update attempt
affectedSystems: Center and driver displays, separate identities
Infotainment software, controllers and low-voltage supply

before.title: R1T / R1S Front Seat Belt Anchor Recall (22V-641, 207 Vehicles)
before.description: NHTSA recall 22V-641 covers approximately 198 R1T and 9 R1S model year 2022 vehicles produced between January 28, 2022 and August 8, 2022 for front seat belt anchors inadequately attached to the B-pillar. Improperly secured anchors may not restrain occupants during a crash. Owners may notice rattling noises from the height-adjuster area of the B-pillar if a bolt is loose.
before.solution: Free recall remedy via Rivian Mobile Service Technician or Rivian Service Center — anchor inspection and proper securing. ~1 hour. Schedule via 1-855-748-4265. Confirm VIN against 22V-641.

proposal.title: R1T / R1S Front Seat Belt Anchor Recall (22V-641, 207 Vehicles)
proposal.description: NHTSA recall 22V-641 / Rivian FSAM-924 covers 207 model-year 2022 vehicles: 198 R1Ts and 9 R1Ss built from January 28 through August 8, 2022. A front driver and/or passenger seat-belt height-adjuster bolt may have been cross-threaded, weakening the attachment to the B-pillar. A loose assembly may rattle at the height-adjuster area or move excessively, and may not restrain an occupant as intended in a crash. These are campaign-population counts, not owner reports.
proposal.solution: Check the VIN for recall 22V-641 / FSAM-924 and schedule Rivian service promptly if open. Rivian Mobile Service or a Rivian Service Center will inspect and, as necessary, properly secure the seat-belt anchorage free of charge; the owner notice estimates about one hour. Do not pull-test or disassemble the anchor. Do not buy a belt, bolt or height adjuster from this page; the recall remedy and any parts depend on VIN and Rivian inspection.
symptoms: Rattle near the front seat-belt height adjuster on the B-pillar
Excessive movement while adjusting front seat-belt height
affectedSystems: Front driver and passenger seat-belt height-adjuster anchorage
